about: Test vectors for the watchOS app's Swift port of the feed's decoder and rules, beyond watch-rules-vectors.json, written by SwiftPortVectorsTest.kt from Kotlin's own answers (plan 4, Task 1). decode: texts a watch may be handed: the four samples by file, the English sample with one change (olderPhone to quotedRtl, notJson and newerPhone apart), newerPhone, a later phone's: the twelve-hour English sample with the first sample's phrases and a key no build reads, future, in every kind of object the feed holds, each of the model's twelve classes once, the countdown phrases, the screens' words, the face screen's words, one of their counts and day 0's 12-hour times among them (Ruling 60 item 1d), the lenient cases (quotedFajr to quotedTarget, Ruling 57 item 2), each oneDay with one more field the port reads written in a wrong type kotlinx reads leniently, plan 3's keys as kotlinx refuses them (nullScreens to numberClockTime, Ruling 57 item 4), the phone's Show sunrise (sunriseHidden, oneDay with ui.showSunrise false, and nullShowSunrise, with it null; olderPhone has no such key and shows Sunrise), the feeds the later sections run on (turkishIkindi, englishIkindi, noMidnights, tromsoMay, and Ruling 57's ishaAtTheNextFajr, aDayOfOneMinute, ishaFirstInADayOfOneMinute, startsAtTheEndOfTime, emptySpokenHours, emptySpokenMinutes, the labels' turkishIkindiTagged to greekTonos, and plan 4 Task 3's blankWords and clockForms), newerShape, and the texts on oneDay, the sample cut to its first day: missingVersion and newerDayShape (at version 2, its times a list), the number and text forms from fractionalVersion to escapedVersionKey, each oneDay with one change (escapedKeyFractionalWrittenAt is fractionalWrittenAt with its key's first letter written as a Unicode escape), the laterKeys cases, oneDay with keys a later phone may add at version 1, named like the integer fields at paths the model does not have, and the duplicate cases, oneDay with one key written a second time. A case's text is json, or the whole text of file, a file in this directory, after a UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF) where bom is true. The mark is a field of its own because Foundation's JSONSerialization drops a U+FEFF that opens a string value (JSONDecoder keeps it). result is what a Wear watch makes of it (FeedStore): feed when WatchFeedJson.decode reads it, newer when it does not and WatchFeedJson.versionOf reads a version above 1, and malformed otherwise. A newer feed need not have this build's shape (newerShape, newerDayShape), so the version is read before the body. class: each case has one (Ruling 56), which this rule gives from its text alone (a file's without the line end it closes with), and SwiftPortVectorsTest holds every case to it. FOREIGN when kotlinx's encoder, configured as WatchFeedJson's, writes no such text: kotlinx's own reader reads no JSON from it (notJson, a trailing comma, a byte-order mark), or the encoder, writing back the JSON kotlinx reads from it, writes another text (an integer written with an exponent or as 1792303200.0, a key spelled with an escape, a key written twice), or a number at one of the model's integer fields (the root's version and writtenAt, a day's midnight and times, an upTo of a spoken or screen count, a phrase's target, an Int or a Long in every model the plans name) has a point or an exponent (1.0, 2.0, 100.0). Otherwise ENCODER when the text holds a value of a model the plans name: a version above 1, whatever the rest (a newer phone's: version2, newerShape, newerDayShape), or a version of 1 with every key the model has holding a value of its field (an Int a whole number in 32 bits, a Long in 64, a Double a number, a Boolean true or false, a String a string, a Char a string of one UTF-16 unit, null only where the field is nullable) and every key without a default there, any other key a later phone's and ignored (newerPhone, and the laterKeys cases, named like the integer fields at paths the model does not have), and a defaulted key free to be absent, as an older phone leaves it (olderPhone). Where the model is this build's, the text is WatchFeedJson.encode's own; an older or a later phone's is the same encoder writing its JSON tree. Otherwise ONE_CHANGE: an ENCODER case's text with one value changed, removed or set to null (version0, missingVersion, noDays, nullInADefaultedField, twoCharacterZero, the four quoted cases, the lenient cases, nullScreens, nullLatinScript, twoCharacterRingZero, numberClockTime, nullShowSunrise, booleanVersion, wideVersion, wideTarget, and the three digitZero cases of two UTF-16 units). The port is held by class. On ENCODER and ONE_CHANGE it answers exactly swift where it is given and result elsewhere, and for a feed decodes exactly expect. swift is on the four quoted cases and the lenient cases alone, each a value of the wrong type that kotlinx reads leniently as its value and the port refuses: a number or a boolean written as a string (kotlinx's consumeNumericLiteral for an Int or a Long, consumeStringLenient and Double.parseDouble for a Double, consumeBooleanLenient for a Boolean), and a Char written as a bare digit (decodeChar's consumeStringLenient). Each is an accepted difference in the safe direction (the Lead's call 8, Ruling 57 item 2): no phone writes a wrong type, and a refusal keeps the last feed the watch understood. There is one lenient case for each field the port reads that kotlinx would read so, plan 3's among them since the port reads them (plan 4 Task 3: quotedTurnRightUpTo, quotedTurnLeftUpTo, bareRingDigitZero, which writes the bare 0 where oneDay has null, and quotedLatinScript), and quotedShowSunrise for the phone's Show sunrise. On FOREIGN it must not crash or hang, and where it answers feed, every value it read is exactly the JSON value the text holds, with no truncation or rounding and the Int32 and Int64 ranges checked, as far as Foundation's Decimal keeps a number's digits: about 38 significant digits, past which a FOREIGN number may read as its rounded whole value (Ruling 57 item 1; ENCODER and ONE_CHANGE texts hold plain integers, so they are unaffected). A refusal is always a right answer there. result and expect are Kotlin's answer, kept as information, which the port is not held to. So the port reads the version first, a version above 1 being newer before the body is read, then decodes with Foundation's JSONDecoder, Kotlin's Int an Int32, a Long an Int64 and digitZero one UTF-16 unit, and needs no JSON scanner of its own (Ruling 56 item 4). Kotlin on the FOREIGN texts, as information: kotlinx refuses an integer field written with a point, and reads one written with an exponent when its value is whole, its digits read into a Long (so a mantissa beyond a Long is malformed) and the exponent applied in double arithmetic, which judges whether the value is whole; it reads a key with its escapes undone, refuses a trailing comma and a mark before the text, and reads every copy of a key written twice as its field and keeps the last, where Foundation's readers keep the first. It skips the value of a key the model lacks with skipElement, which balances its brackets and reads each string in it with its escapes checked, so a bad escape there is malformed and other text that is not JSON there is not. And it reads forms Foundation refuses (leading zeros, capital booleans, a raw tab, line break or NUL in a string, a lone surrogate, and 23., .5 or 1e-400 for a Double), which no case holds. For a feed, expect is what Kotlin decodes: the number of days, day 0's hijriDayMonth, gregorianSpoken and midnight (null with no day), ui.digitZero, ui.ringDigitZero (null for none), ui.latinScript, ui.showSunrise, day0Asr (day 0's Asr as WatchRules.clockText draws it and WatchRules.spokenClock says it, null with no day), whether ui.spoken is there, the number of his phrases, and the city. Every case of spoken, labels, days, clock, words, moments and starts names its feed, a decode case, and carries that case's class, always ENCODER: the port gives exactly its answer. The cases of filled, inDigits and contract are no feeds and carry no class: the port gives exactly Kotlin's answer on each. spoken: WatchRules.spokenCountdown(feed, name, clock, secondsLeft) for day 0's Asr, its name and its time as WatchRules.spokenClock gives it; null for a feed with no spoken words, or with an empty list of spoken hours or minutes (emptySpokenHours, emptySpokenMinutes). labels: the prayer's name on that day in capitals, uppercased by ui.language's tag, as ComplicationFields.nextPrayer writes it (Turkish capitalises i as İ): on the JVM, by the language Locale.forLanguageTag reads from the tag, its primary subtag in any case, so tr-u-ca-gregory is Turkish and AZ Azerbaijani, and tr_TR, ill-formed, is no language; and only Turkish, Azerbaijani and Lithuanian (its dot above dropped) case otherwise than the default, where Foundation's ICU also cases Greek its own way (its tonos dropped), so greekTonos is the default's (Ruling 57 item 6). Day 6 of each sample is Friday 23 October, whose Dhuhr is the Jumuʿah. days: WatchRules.today(feed, now) and WatchRules.dayStart(feed, today), null when now is on no day of the feed, a second before, at and after the start of each day named and on both sides of the last day's end. sample turns over at its midnights; noMidnights has none, so its dates turn over at solar midnight, halfway between two Dhuhrs; tromsoMay is the high-latitude night. clock: each of the six times of days 0 and 6, keyed by WatchTime (Sunrise among them), as WatchRules.clockText draws it and as WatchRules.spokenClock splices it into a spoken line: a 12-hour time with its day period, isolated by U+2068 and U+2069 when spoken; a 24-hour time, in any digits, the same both ways. On clockForms, days 0, 1 and 2: clock strings in Bengali, extended Arabic-Indic and Devanagari digits, said as they are, and in the mathematical bold digits, each two UTF-16 units that Kotlin's Char.isDigit does not take, so isolated; 12-hour times with the marker first, a narrow no-break space, and none; and on day 2 (Ruling 60 item 1a) clock strings in numbers that are no decimal digit (Unicode's No and Nl: superscript and circled digits, circled numbers, the Roman numeral ten), each one UTF-16 unit Char.isDigit does not take, so isolated: a digit is a decimal digit, Nd, never any number. A clock time is the phone's string, a 12-hour phone's day period the one its clockTime carries (Ruling 58 item 3). words: WatchFeed.words(), the feed's ui.screens with the English for every word left blank, written whole with every key, on the four samples, olderPhone (no words, so all English) and blankWords. Blank is Kotlin's isBlank: empty, or every UTF-16 unit a Char.isWhitespace (a space separator, a line or paragraph separator, tab to carriage return, U+001C to U+001F, each of the four alone in a word of blankWords), so U+0085 and U+200B are words; a list is English only when empty; the presets are the English map overlaid by the feed's names that are not blank, an id the English lacks kept. presetIds (Ruling 60 item 1e): the presets' ids in Kotlin's order, which a dictionary does not keep: TasbeehPresets.builtIn's, whatever order the phone sent them in, then each id they lack in the order the phone sent it (blankWords sends custom_2, alhamdulillah, subhanallah and custom_1, and its ids end custom_2, custom_1). moments (Ruling 57 item 5): a rules case in watch-rules-vectors.json's shape (WatchRules.moment's next, previous, secondsLeft and progress, the Float widened to a Double, so exact; countdown, litOnList and litOnGlance) at instants no earlier case reached: on ishaAtTheNextFajr, the sample's first two days with day 0's Isha moved onto day 1's Fajr, around that instant, where yesterday's starts count only before today's Fajr; and on aDayOfOneMinute, the same two days with day 1 beginning a minute after day 0, before day 0's Fajr, where no start has arrived when the date has turned, so the previous is yesterday's Isha, still ahead, and the progress 0; on ishaFirstInADayOfOneMinute, with that Isha before its Fajr, it is the next start too, a period of no length, whose progress is 0 by the guard (the time since that Isha, negative, over 0 is -Infinity); and on startsAtTheEndOfTime, the same two days with every time at Long.MAX_VALUE - 1000 and day 1 beginning at Long.MIN_VALUE + 100000, ten seconds in: the previous is yesterday's Isha and the next today's Fajr, at one instant more than half of a Long ahead, a period of no length whose time since its start wraps to a positive number, as a Long does, so the progress is 0 by the guard alone, which read total < 0 would leave +Infinity, and the clamp 1. starts: WatchRules.starts whole, on ishaAtTheNextFajr and tromsoMay: a start at or after the next day's Fajr is left out. filled: WatchRules.filled(pattern, parts): each place %n$s replaced by the nth part, in any order and more than once, a part never filled in turn, and a place that names no part (%0$s, one beyond the parts, one beyond an Int) kept as it is. inDigits: WatchRules.inDigits(text, zero): each Western digit written as the digit that many places after zero, added in 16 bits as Kotlin's Char does, so from U+FFFA the 6 is U+0000; other text kept. contract: WatchLinkContract's context and message keys and its byte figures; isFingerprint; deliveryOf on each text, with the delivery it reads (origin, seq as an Int64, fingerprint) or none; stores(held, arriving), held absent when the watch holds nothing; echoOf(held); and the order a receiver stores in, STORE_STEPS (Ruling 50). The delivery travels beside the feed and never inside it, so no decode text holds one. The contract's cases are not feeds and carry no class: the port gives exactly Kotlin's answer on each. Nobody edits this file: change the Kotlin, then rewrite it with ./gradlew :watchcore:testAndroidHostTest -Ptaqwa.updateVectors and commit the result.
